A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EgoEverything, with directly matchable methods, equations, experiments and figures. All 11 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2 are readable. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; v1 has unresolved appendix references.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original VLM evaluations, human accuracy, text-only tests and analyses of recall interval, object size and gaze distance.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the original evaluations and adds a saliency-map prompting result. Section 3.2 also reports a qualitative clustering-parameter comparison.

M1.justification: The three-stage pipeline, Gaussian target sampling, CLIP-based re-identification, question-generation agents and filtering remain. V1 already specifies real gaze data in Section 3.2; v2's corrected terminology and fuller clustering description do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the AEA/Nymeria-derived benchmark with the same question and object categories. No additional dataset, domain or language is evaluated. The newly discussed gaze-aware benchmarks provide related-work context or a prompting protocol, not additional evaluation data.

E2.justification: V2 adds a saliency-map-based gaze prompting comparator on VideoLLaMA3-7B, following EgoGazeVQA. The models and FR, AD, GC, GM, VMP and AMEGO comparisons in Table 1, and the text-only comparators in Table 2, remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 introduces the saliency-map input evaluation and reports testing K values of 8, 12 and 16 for clustering. Existing preprocessing comparisons, the 400-pixel sampling parameter and the three-minute minimum questioning delay are retained.

E4.justification: Section 3.2 adds a qualitative sensitivity comparison of clustering granularity, reporting better question quality with K=12. The recall, gaze-distance and object-size analyses already existed in v1 Figure 7 and largely reappear in v2 Table 3; the illustrated MCQ cases are also retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added comparison continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 reports 51.19% accuracy for the new saliency-map prompting condition; the existing VideoLLaMA3-7B FR score remains 49.1%. Tables 1 and 2 otherwise retain their scores, including 83.5% human accuracy. V2 also newly reports K=12 as best for downstream question quality.

T1.justification: The Gaussian sampling equation is unchanged, and neither version supplies theoretical proofs. Separating the minimum delay from the realized recall interval clarifies notation already implicit in v1's sampling range and Figure 7, without changing the mathematical procedure.

C1.justification: V2 qualifies the central attention claim: measured gaze supplies a weak attention prior rather than directly representing user intention. The core contribution remains the same gaze-aware AR benchmark and generation pipeline, with the same claimed scale and model–human performance gap.

C2.justification: V2 removes the standalone limitations covering omitted attention modalities, English-only questions, restricted domains and fixed-Gaussian generalizability. It adds substantive interpretations of the broad spatial prior and attributes long-recall difficulty to redundancy, distractors and episode retrieval rather than insufficient video-length capacity.

D1.justification: V2 documents K=12, temporal smoothing over a ±5-frame window, a two-second minimum segment duration, source-video resolutions and data rates, and question-category definitions. It also supplies a dataset-release URL. These additions replace unresolved appendix pointers and expand documentation without establishing reruns.

R1.justification: V2 adds focused discussion of EgoGazeVQA, GazeVQA and StreamGaze, distinguishing offline gaze-based target selection from supplying gaze during querying. Additional AR hardware and eye-tracking citations support the expanded deployment motivation; the existing related-work framework remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion receive targeted rewrites, with expanded background and construction explanations. Terminology and agent abbreviations are corrected, and unresolved appendix references are replaced with inline material. The principal section order and much of the narrative remain.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to a single-column template, substantially resizing and relocating figures and tables. Figure 1(b) changes its illustration, Figure 3 updates agent labels, examples and distributions move, and v1 Figure 7 becomes v2 Table 3.

improvement.justification: V2 resolves the misleading simulated-gaze wording and supplies construction details previously deferred to unresolved appendices, improving interpretability and reproducibility. The added gaze-prompting comparison and closer related-work positioning provide useful support. Removing explicit limitations weakens transparency, but the documentation gains yield a modest overall improvement; the main empirical evidence remains stable.
